text:
Chicago won 5-3, but the way the game was played says Pittsburgh should have taken it. The Penguins out-attempted the Blackhawks 61 to 34 and owned the even-strength chances, 2.67 expected goals to 1.54. Over simulated replays of every shot, PIT wins this game 76 percent of the time. The night turned on a few finishes: Teuvo Teravainen's wrist shot at 15:42 of the third, a 1 percent chance, put CHI up 4-3 after Sidney Crosby had tied it.

Chicago started fastest. Teravainen scored 28 seconds in, and Roman Kantserov converted a power play late in the first for a 2-1 lead. The Penguins took over in the second, generating 1.96 expected goals to Chicago's 0.74, yet Kantserov's snap shot at 10:32 made it 3-1 anyway. Nick Robertson cut the gap to one at 17:51. Crosby, who scored twice, tied it at 3-3 on a 44 percent chance in the third. Sergei Murashov allowed four goals on 1.98 expected, a swing of 2.02 goals against him, while Spencer Knight stopped 24 of 27 and held roughly even with the quality of shots he faced.

The finish was cruel. Teravainen's long shot gave CHI the lead, and Tyler Bertuzzi added a tip-in at 19:50 on an 88 percent chance to seal it. Teravainen, with two goals and an assist, took first star, and Kantserov's two goals earned second. Chicago also went 1 for 2 on the power play while Pittsburgh went 0 for 4, a quiet but real difference in a game decided by small margins.
